articles.title: Cube-based screening identifies a quinoa-derived synthetic microbial community that promotes plant growth and modulates root epidermal responses under salt stress.
articles.abstract: Plant-associated bacteria can improve plant performance under abiotic stress, but beneficial functions in plant microbiomes may depend on defined combinations of microorganisms rather than individual isolates alone. Here, we developed a cube-based screening strategy to identify functional synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) from 135 quinoa-associated bacterial isolates while preserving combinatorial diversity and traceability of isolate-level contributions. The isolates were divided into five 27-isolate sets, each arranged as a 3 × 3 × 3 cube in which each 3 × 3 layer was defined as a 9-isolate SynCom, generating 45 SynComs in total. Screening under 100 mM NaCl identified SynCom DY1 (SCDY1) as a candidate salt stress-mitigating consortium. SCDY1 consisted of nine taxonomically diverse isolates and exhibited a multifunctional profile, including siderophore production, phosphate solubilization, carboxymethyl cellulose degradation, indole compound production, and growth under saline conditions. articles.title: Protective effect of glyburide on wound healing in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats via alteration of NF-κB/transforming growth factor-β and cellular jun/platelet-derived growth factor-vascular endothelial growth factor signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: Diabetes-induced abnormal wound healing is characterized by prolonged oxidative stress, inflammation, and impaired tissue regeneration, largely due to excessive production of oxidative stress and inflammatory mediators. Glyburide is a well-known antidiabetic drug. In this experimental study, we scrutinized the protective effect of glyburide against streptozotocin (STZ) induced wound healing in rats and explored the underlying mechanism.

articles.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease associated with periodontal tissue destruction and bone loss. Libidibia ferrea presents antibacterial, anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties with potential therapeutic relevance.

articles.title: Pharmacogenomic Markers of Disease Susceptibility and Glucocorticoid Responsiveness in Pemphigus Vulgaris.
articles.abstract: Response to glucocorticoid (GC) therapy in pemphigus vulgaris (PV) is variable and may be influenced by pharmacogenomic factors. This study aimed to evaluate the association between glutathione S-transferases (GST) gene polymorphisms and Multidrug resistance protein 1 (MDR1) or ATP-binding cassette sub-family B member 1 (ABCB1) variations with steroid responsiveness in PV patients and evaluate their role in conferring susceptibility to PV.

articles.title: Tea Polyphenol EGCG Prevents UVB-Induced Oxidative Stress via SIRT3-Mediated Activation of SOD2: Mechanistic Insights from Molecular Interactions.
articles.abstract: UVB irradiation triggers skin photodamage via oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. This study investigated the photoprotective mechanism of EGCG, the most abundant polyphenol in green tea, in HaCaT keratinocytes. EGCG pretreatment attenuated UVB-induced viability loss and oxidative stress, evidenced by reduced 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal, protein carbonyls, and ROS, alongside restored glutathione redox balance. EGCG recovered SIRT3 enzymatic activity without affecting its expression and promoted SOD2 deacetylation at Lys68 and Lys122 in vitro. SPR and ITC confirmed direct, high-affinity binding of EGCG to SIRT3, with molecular dynamics simulations revealing a stable complex. EGCG also enhanced the binding affinity between SIRT3 and its acetylated p53 substrate in vitro. Critically, pharmacological inhibition of SIRT3 by 3-TYP abolished EGCG's protective effects, supporting a critical role of SIRT3 in EGCG-mediated protection. Collectively, these findings indicate that EGCG protects against UVB-induced skin photodamage by binding to and activating SIRT3, thereby promoting SIRT3-mediated SOD2 deacetylation to alleviate oxidative stress.

articles.title: Ferroptosis-Related GPX4 and CD71 and Immune Checkpoint PD-L1 in Cutaneous Melanoma: Associations with Clinicopathologic Features and Survival Outcomes.
articles.abstract: Ferroptosis-related pathways and immune checkpoint signaling may contribute to melanoma progression, but their clinicopathologic and prognostic interplay remains incompletely characterized. To investigate GPX4, CD71, and PD-L1 expression in primary cutaneous melanoma and evaluate their associations with clinicopathologic features and survival outcomes. This retrospective single-center cohort included 44 patients with primary cutaneous melanoma. PD-L1, GPX4, and CD71 expressions were assessed immunohistochemically. Associations with clinicopathologic parameters were analyzed, and overall survival (OS) and disease-free survival (DFS) were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses.
